metadata.iteration: P32 — the first review suite. Routing graded from .dispatch-log; option B (the honesty of an unavailable dispatch) graded as an alternation.
metadata.scope: REPORTING-AND-ROUTING-ONLY. A subagent cannot spawn subagents, so Task did not exist in any of these runs and no reviewer-* was ever actually dispatched. These runs measure which reviewers were DRAWN and what the report SAID about the dispatch — not the fan-out.
metadata.option_a_status: NEVER RUN. The top-level arm (real dispatch, from a session that is not a subagent) is documented as a manual runbook step in evals/README.md and has not been executed.
metadata.token_note: tokens and tool calls are the harness-reported subagent totals per Agent call, not a self-estimate (P18).
metadata.grader_revision: These runs were executed and first graded against the grader as opened in PR #82. A bot review then found three assertions satisfiable by a report asserting their opposite; the grader was tightened and ALL THREE saved workdirs were re-graded unchanged — 13/13 again. The numbers below hold under the tightened grader.

headline: 3 of 3 runs green, 13 of 13 assertions. The suite's value here is negative evidence — no assertion reddened a correct run — and the discrimination is carried by the five committed cheats and the seven-spelling battery, not by these runs. One near-miss is the finding worth keeping: eval 2's run drew ALL THREE reviewers, so an assertion that reviewer-performance must NOT be drawn on that diff would have failed the first real run it ever saw.

notes: Routed as the skill's docs/comment-only case: correctness alone, and both skipped lenses named with the rule that skipped them.

Found two High findings in the prose itself (documented uniqueness does not survive the documented 80-character CMS truncation; the 'what is not handled' section names the loud empty-string case and omits the silent one) — it ran the code to check the claims rather than reading them.
Disclosed the fallback although eval 1 does not assert it: 'the correctness lens below was executed directly in this context'.

THE NEAR-MISS: it drew all three, not the two the ideal outcome draws. The suite asserts only that security was drawn here; had it also asserted that performance was NOT, this run would have been red and the assertion wrong.
Confirmed the injection end-to-end against a throwaway copy rather than asserting it, and flagged the committed token as a second Critical.
Disclosure spelling: 'all three lenses synthesized here in one context since dispatch returns no findings'.
The only run unambiguously executed against the PRE-clause SKILL.md (its report was written 3m20s before the option-B clause was added), so its disclosure is the unprompted behaviour P32 predicted.

Disclosure spelling: 'All three lenses were therefore applied by the synthesizing context itself, not by three independent adversarial reviewers. That is strictly weaker than a real dispatch: one context, one set of blind spots, no disagreement to surface.'
Volunteered the Option A recommendation itself: it closed by saying a real three-reviewer dispatch should be re-run.

limitations: No dispatch was exercised. Not by omission — it cannot be, from a subagent.
One run per eval, so nothing here is a variance measurement.

3 of 3 green on first contact means these runs did not discriminate. They are evidence that the assertions do not redden correct behaviour; the evidence that they CAN fail is the five cheats and the battery.
Runs 1 and 2 were launched before the option-B clause was added to SKILL.md and finished after it, so it is not established which text they read. Only run 3 is clean pre-clause evidence.
The three runs were graded twice: once under the grader as first opened, once under the tightened one. Same result both times, but they were not produced against the final grader.
